findings.reason: §9 should be collapsed to its one live item (the §7 stopgap lift) or a node pays to rebuild work already merged.
findings.text: §9's "next, in order" lists §3 then §4 as open work, but §3's cross-harness resume ("a run redispatched to another harness and then resumed breaks") is already implemented by the harness-ownership check in `_task_session_resolution` (dispatch.py:11484, `owner != harness` withholds) and `_current_harness_session` (dispatch.py:11592), and both §3 and §4 are declared done and recorded met by the 2026-10-01 currency audit — so a node dispatched against §9 re-derives landed machinery

findings.reason: the honest change is to call `runs.capture_run_session` at those four sites and delete the shim, rather than keep a parallel entry point named for the contract this plan retires.
findings.text: `_capture_member_session(record)` forwards unchanged to `capture_run_session` (reckon/crew/runs.py:79) and carries the retired "member" vocabulary the plan's whole design removes, yet is reached from `reckon/crew/promotion.py:5365`, `:8169`, `:8680` and `dispatch.py:11125`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the dispatch-time decision is one entry point, `_task_session_resolution` (dispatch.py:11426), hiding the record shape (committed rows + live pointers), the task-identity join and the disqualification, behind a two-key return and delegating resolution to `resume.resolve_session`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the design extends the session-resolution owner (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:464 resolve_session`) and the member-liveness owner (`reckon/crew/node.py:357 member_in_flight_verdict`) rather than forking either; `_prior_same_task_run` (dispatch.py:11347) is about run selection, not a second session reader.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the implementable sections add no public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family — §2's absence names are `point` reasons recorded on the run (`session_absence`), not refusal codes — and the sections do name what they retire (the roster session write and the shared session member).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched broadly (§1's 34-row reuse map; §2−§6 reuse `resumption.resolve_session`, `runs.capture_run_session`, `node.member_in_flight_verdict` and `rollout.read_rollout_receipt`). §9, however, schedules as implementable the §3 and §4 work whose mechanism already exists at `dispatch.py:11484`/`dispatch.py:11592` and which section declarations `s3=done`, `s4=done` record as landed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `_capture_member_session` is a pure forwarder over the run-capture owner with no behaviour and no justification.
